summary: Henk Bodewitz was an Indologist who completed his degrees and PhD at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda. He taught Sanskrit at Utrecht University (assistant professor 1966, chair 1976–1992) and held associate (ca. 1971–1976) and full professorships (1992–2002) at Leiden University.

Henri Bergson was a philosopher who studied at Lycée Condorcet, École Normale Supérieure (ca. 1878–1881), and the University of Paris (ca. 1888–1889). His career included posts at the lycée David d'Angers (ca. 1881–1883) and the Collège de France (1900–1904).

Henri Cordier was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Lycée Chaptal. He served as a professor at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales from ca. 1881 to 1925 and at Sciences Po from ca. 1886 to 1925.

Henri Gaidoz was a linguist who studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and under Albrecht Weber in 1865. He taught geography and ethnography at Sciences Po (1872–1908) and served as director of studies for Celtic philology at École Pratique des Hautes Études (1876).

Henri Hubert studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure (ca. 1892–1895), working in religious studies and history/archaeology. He held positions at the National Archaeological Museum (ca. 1898–1927), École Pratique des Hautes Études (ca. 1901–1927), and École du Louvre (ca. 1906–1927).

Henri Maspero was a scholar of sinology, linguistics, and religion who studied under Édouard Chavannes and at INALCO. He held posts at EFEO, Collège de France (1918–1945), EPHE (ca. 1920–1945), Maison Franco-Japonaise (1928–1930), and the University of Paris (ca. 1937–1945).

Henri Massé was an Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar and linguist. He held academic posts at the University of Algiers from ca. 1916 to 1927 and at École des langues orientales from ca. 1927 to 1958.

Henri Pirenne was a historian who studied at the University of Liège, Ghent University, Berlin, Leipzig, University of Paris, and EPHE. He held posts at the University of Liège (ca. 1885–1886) and Ghent University (1886–1931 as Professor of History).

Henrik Samuel Nyberg was a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and religious studies who studied at Uppsala University in 1908. He taught at Fjellstedt School (ca. 1912–1919) and served as docent and professor of Semitics at Uppsala University (ca. 1919–1956).

Henry Beveridge, an Indologist and historian, was educated at the University of Glasgow and Queen's University Belfast. He served in the Indian Civil Service from 1857 to 1893 and was president of The Asiatic Society from 1890 to 1891.

Henry Clarke Warren worked in Buddhist studies and Indology, studying at Harvard, Johns Hopkins, and Oxford, under Charles Rockwell Lanman, Maurice Bloomfield, and T. W. Rhys Davids. He founded the Harvard Oriental Series in 1891.

Henry George Keene was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar educated at Fort William College and Sidney Sussex College, Cambridge. After serving in the East India Company (ca. 1798–1811), he became Professor of Arabic, Persian, and Hindústání Literature at East India Company College (1824–1834).

Henry Hamilton Hadley was a religious studies and linguistics scholar educated at Yale and Andover and Union theological seminaries. He served at Yale Divinity School (1861) and held instructor (1858) and professorial (1862) positions in Hebrew and sacred literature at Union Theological Seminary.

Henry Herbert Dodwell was a historian and Indologist educated at Lord Williams's School and St John's College, Oxford. He served in the Indian Education Service (1908–1922) and was Professor of History and Culture of the British Dominions in Asia at SOAS (1922–1946).

Henry M. Hoenigswald was a linguist who studied at the universities of Munich, Zurich, Padua, and Florence between 1932 and 1936. He served on the faculty at the University of Pennsylvania from ca. 1948 to 1985.

Henry Martyn was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies. He was educated at Truro Cathedral School, St John's College (ca. 1797–1801), and studied under John Borthwick Gilchrist around 1804–1805.
Henry Miers Elliot, an Indologist and historian, was educated at Winchester College. He served as a civil servant with the East India Company from ca. 1826 to 1853.

Henry Pitts Forster was an Indologist and linguist. He served in the Bengal Civil Service and East India Company from 1783 to 1815, and was appointed Master of the Calcutta Mint at the India Government Mint, Kolkata, in 1803.

Henry Rawlinson was a linguist, historian, and Iranian studies scholar educated at Great Ealing School and Middlesex University. He served with the East India Company (ca. 1827–1856), the Foreign Office (ca. 1859–1860), and held leadership roles at the RGS and RAS.

Henry Shiu is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his PhD from the University of Toronto in 2006. He studied under Shek-wing Tam, Leonard C. D. C. Priestley, David Waterhouse, and Willard Gurdon Oxtoby.
